feedback: If a learner describes the device as 'making' movement or light, ask what went IN to make that happen and trace the chain back to the source (chemical energy in the battery, elastic energy you wound in, sunlight falling on the cup) — nothing is created.

If a learner names only the output ('it buzzes', 'it lights up'), prompt 'where did the energy for that come from?' to draw out the full input→output chain, and have them point to the part where the energy is transferred to the output.
If a learner swaps parts at random when it underperforms, ask what exactly is going wrong first, then change one thing and re-test — model fair, targeted iteration.
Ask: could the device run forever without the battery, or without re-winding it? Use the 'no' to reinforce that the energy comes from a finite starting store or an ongoing supply like sunlight.
Prompt: is any energy going somewhere you didn't intend, like heat or sound? Not all the input becomes the useful output.
activities.intendedInsight: A device moves energy from a starting source to a useful output — it never makes energy from nothing — and the first build is meant to be improved: targeted test-and-refine, not random tinkering, is the point of the task.
learnerActions: Take a design brief with a measurable-enough goal, e.g. 'make the buggy cross this line', 'warm the water in the cup', or 'make the buzzer sound'.

Choose an energy source and a matching converter from real kit: a battery with a motor, bulb or buzzer; a wound elastic band turning an axle and wheels; sunlight on a black cup (or foil reflector); or moving air turning windmill blades; plus parts (wheels, card, black cup, foil).
Build a first version, then TEST it against the goal and record what actually happened (did it cross the line? how far? how warm?).
State the energy story out loud: name where the energy starts and the useful output, e.g. 'stored chemical energy in the battery → the motor turns → the wheels move'.
Identify ONE specific weakness from the test evidence, change just that one thing (fresher/bigger source, lighter load), and re-test to see if it improved.

Point to the part where the energy is transferred to the useful output (e.g. the motor, where the electric current makes it spin), and name any energy that spread to the surroundings (e.g. the motor got warm, or some light or sound was wasted).
activities.title: Design, build and refine a real energy-converting device

feedback: For a matching error, prompt the learner to say the energy story aloud and re-check the starting source.
If the loop is mis-ordered, ask what you must do before you can refine something (build and test it first).
activities.intendedInsight: Secure recall that devices convert from a named source, and that engineering follows a repeating design→build→test→refine loop.
learnerActions: Match each device to its input→output conversion (device → conversion).
Put the steps of the design loop in order: design → build → test → refine.
Answer 'where does the energy come from?' style questions, choosing the starting source.
activities.title: Consolidation: match devices to conversions and order the design loop
